basis: Axonal neuropathy with demonstrated mitochondrial respiratory-chain dysfunction; fixed pes cavus in 37/44 (84%). Bladder dysfunction only 1/44.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: mitochondrial respiratory-chain dysfunction is demonstrated by reduced complex activities in 2/3, supporting an energy-metabolism disorder.

basis: Developmental impairment and characteristic skeletal hypoplasia/contractures define syndrome; visual dysfunction 30-79%. Renal/biliary defects mostly 5-29%; pilomatrixoma is separate.

decisions.dermatologic: none: pilomatrixoma is a separately diagnosed associated neoplasm, despite its annotated frequency of 30-79%.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: skeletal abnormalities, including distal phalangeal hypoplasia and contractures, are characteristic components of the syndrome's definition.

basis: Mitochondrial cardiomyopathy; muscle weakness 1/2 with atrophy/myopathic biopsy 1/1; intellectual disability 1/1. Cataract 1/1 omitted by cap; evidence comprises very few patients.

decisions.neurologic: involved: intellectual disability is reported in 1/1 assessed patient; retain lifelong neurodevelopmental impairment under the cap, with substantial sampling uncertainty.
decisions.ocular: none: cataract in 1/1 assessed patient qualifies by supplied frequency but is omitted under the four-axis cap.

basis: Trypanosomal infection with defining CNS invasion (80-99% neurologic abnormalities); infection-related anemia is common (~30%+). ECG changes alone do not establish common cardiac injury.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: ECG abnormalities occur in 30-79%, but substantial myocardial or conduction-system injury is not established at that frequency; AV block is 5-29%.
decisions.neurologic: primary: the characteristic meningoencephalitic stage defines sleeping sickness; neurologic abnormalities occur in 80-99%.

basis: Defining skeletal, brain and atrophic skin defects; microphthalmia 30-79%, iris coloboma 40%. Bowel malrotation 40% and chronic constipation 30% omitted by cap.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: malrotation 4/10 and chronic constipation 3/10 support gastrointestinal involvement, but the axis is omitted under the four-axis cap.
decisions.ocular: involved: microphthalmia occurs in 30-79% and iris coloboma in 4/10; retain common structural eye abnormalities under the cap.

basis: Adrenal steroid synthesis deficiency; urethral hypospadias occurs in 30-79% and falls within the renal axis. Hormonal salt wasting does not establish intrinsic kidney injury.

decisions.renal: involved: hypospadias is a structural urethral malformation annotated in 30-79%; the renal axis explicitly includes the urethra. Salt wasting alone would not qualify.

basis: Blood-vessel endothelial neoplasm; most cases (>50%) directly occupy dermis or subcutis, supporting dermatologic involvement.

decisions.dermatologic: involved: the usual presentation is a cutaneous or subcutaneous tumor, accounting for most cases (>50%); this is direct tumor occupation.

basis: Limb reduction and clefts define syndrome; developmental disability and cataract each 30-79%. Sparse hair (80-99%) and cardiovascular anomalies (30-79%) omitted by cap.

decisions.ocular: involved: cataract occurs in 30-79%; retain its potential for substantial visual loss under the four-axis cap.
decisions.dermatologic: none: sparse hair occurs in 80-99%, but its lower functional impact gives it lower priority than neurologic and ocular impairment under the cap.

basis: Rickettsia typhi infects vascular endothelium and causes small-vessel vasculitis; transient rash does not establish skin damage.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: endothelial infection and small-vessel vasculitis are intrinsic disease pathology; vessels belong to the cardiovascular axis.

basis: Arthrogryposis, developmental impairment and characteristic cleft/swallowing dysfunction define syndrome; strabismus 80-99%. Hearing abnormalities 30-79% omitted by cap.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: characteristic cleft palate and persistent swallowing dysfunction are defining features; orofacial cleft occurs in 30-79% and dysphagia in 80-99%.
